selection: Proportional category-stratified random sample of unenriched topics with at least two original tournament source IDs.

topics.description: A bowed string instrument tuned C–G–D–A, pitched between the violin and cello, and commonly played in alto clef as an inner or alto voice in ensembles.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This lower of the two featured instruments in Mozart's E-flat sinfonia concertante (sin-FOH-neeah kahn-sir-TAHN-tay) is labeled “da braccio” (dah BRAH-choh) in the sixth Brandenburg Concerto.  This instrument is usually tuned “C G D A,” unlike a similar instrument called “da gamba.” Parts  for this instrument are typical “inner voices” in Classical (*) quartets and are in the alto clef. This  instrument is the second most numerous in most orchestras, after another instrument also played on the  shoulder. For 10 points, name this bowed instrument pitched between the larger cello and smaller violin.
parts.answer: viola [or viola da braccio; do not accept or prompt on “viola da gamba” or “viol”]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: After woodwinds, this instrument picks up the fugato “The Cuckoo Sat on the Fence” in a concerto based on folk tales. This instrument represents the title character of a work based on its composer’s scrapped Rob Roy Overture that ends with an “orgy of bandits.” Works like Der Schwanendreher [der sch-VAHN-en-dare-ur] were composed for this instrument by Paul (*) Hindemith. This instrument is principal in Hector Berlioz’s Harold in Italy. This is the smaller of two instruments whose lowest string is tuned to C with its other string tuned to G, D, and A. Players of this string instrument read music in alto clef. For 10 points, name this string instrument pitched between a violin and a cello.

topics.description: A plucked-string keyboard instrument in which keys activate jacks to pluck strings; it was prominent in Renaissance and Baroque music and preceded the modern piano.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Polish virtuosa Wanda Landowska (“VAHN-dah lan-DOHV-skah”):

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Landowska commissioned Manuel de Falla to write a concerto for this instrument, which she played. This plucked-string keyboard instrument preceded the modern piano.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Landowska also commissioned this French composer to write his Concert champetre (“kon-SAIR shawm-PET”). This composer wrote the opera Dialogue of the Carmelites and was a member of Les Six alongside Arthur Honegger (“oh-neh-GAIR”) and Darius Milhaud (“mee-YO”).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Landowska made the first modern harpsichord recordings of this composer’s Goldberg Variations. This composer’s Italian Concerto and Well-Tempered Clavier were also recorded by Landowska.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Many of this man's pieces pivot at a central “crux” identified by cataloguer Ralph Kirkpatrick. For  10 points:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this prolific composer of sonatas, whose 555 pieces in that genre are found in books such as  the 30 Essercizi (ez-air-CHEET-see) written for Infanta Maria Barbara.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Scarlatti's sonatas were largely written for this Baroque instrument, a predecessor of the piano that  plucks strings with jacks.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Scarlatti often crossed himself when speaking of this German-born keyboardist who composed The  Harmonious Blacksmith. A piece by this composer repeats “And he shall reign forever and ever.”
parts.answer: George Frideric Handel [or George Frederick Handel; or Georg Friedrich Handel]

topics.description: A 20th-century avant-garde art and literary movement exploring dreams, the unconscious, and unexpected or fantastical juxtapositions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A floating apple obscures the face of a man wearing a bowler hat in one painting from this movement. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this art movement, a Belgian member of whom created artworks such as The Son of Man.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Son of Man was created by this surrealist, who, in The Treachery of Images, declared “this is not a pipe”.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Many Magritte paintings feature a background of this subject. Magritte’s depictions of this subject were usually blue and often featured clouds.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Belgian artist René Magritte:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Magritte was a member of this art movement. Many paintings in this 20th century art movement depict otherworldly subjects or were inspired by dreams.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In this Magritte work, a painting on an easel seems to directly depict the landscape seen through a window behind it. A second painting by Magritte with the same title as this painting features the same concept with a seascape.
parts.answer: The Human Condition [or La condition humaine; accept The Human Condition II or La condition humaine II]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] An enormous one of these objects fills up Magritte’s painting The Listening Room. Another of these objects floats in the air in front of the face of a man wearing a suit in Magritte’s The Son of Man.

topics.description: The human voice is the sound-producing instrument used for speech, singing, choral music, and other vocal performances.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2022, Raven Chacon became the first Native American to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music, with a piece titled for being without this instrument. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] What instrument is used to perform Clara Ward’s “How I Got Over”? Kirk Franklin has won 16 Grammy awards for works featuring this instrument.
parts.answer: human voices [accept Voiceless Mass; accept throats]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Chacon’s piece was a “Voiceless” example of these musical works that set Christian liturgy to music.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In 1996, George Walker became the first Black winner of the Pulizter with a church-inspired setting of “When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d,” a poem also set to music by this composer’s Ode to Death. This man wrote a piece subtitled “The Bringer of Old Age.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a form of Inuit musical performance called katajjaq, two people face each other and perform this instrument in short, rhythmic patterns. The term “fry” is used to refer to the lowest register of notes producible by this instrument. Rhythm is emphasized over pitch in the sprechstimme style of performing this instrument, while highly articulated phrasing is characteristic of its (*) bel canto style. A style of delivery for this instrument is the rectative. This instrument is usually the soloist of arias. For 10 points, performers use namesake chords in their throats to produce the sounds of what instruments used in choirs?
parts.answer: human voice [or singing or vocalizing; accept talking]

topics.description: Spanish painter and printmaker whose works include the Black Paintings, Los Caprichos, The Disasters of War, and The Third of May 1808.
aliases: Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes

parts.label: L
parts.question: This series includes a painting in which two men trapped knee-deep in sand battle with weapons called Fight with Cudgels. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this series of pieces painted directly onto the walls of the artist’s house, the Quinta del Sordo. Another piece in this series, Witches’ Sabbath, depicts Satan in the form of a goat.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This deaf Spanish artist included Saturn Devouring His Son in his Black Paintings.
parts.answer: Francisco Goya [or Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Goya’s The Disasters of War series protests this leader’s invasion of Spain during the Peninsular War. In a Jacques-Louis David painting, this French emperor is depicted crossing the Alps.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about fine art and popular music, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] A 2016 album by Swedish djent band Meshuggah is titled The Violent Sleep of Reason, a reference to this Spanish artist's The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters, one of his Los Caprichos etchings. He also painted The Third of May, 1808.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This American musical artist sang "And how you suffered for your sanity / And how you tried to set them free" in "Vincent", a song addressed to Vincent van Gogh. He is better known for singing about "the day the music died" in "American Pie".

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The pioneering pop artist Richard Hamilton designed the album cover for this band's "White Album". John Lennon and Paul McCartney were both members of this rock band from Liverpool.

topics.topic: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
topics.description: Rembrandt’s 1632 group portrait depicting Nicolaes Tulp conducting an anatomical dissection before fellow surgeons.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a painting by Thomas Eakins, a woman in black sobs into her sleeve while a man with this profession stands in front of a crowded theater with red-stained hands. Rembrandt painted a group of people with this job watching Nicolaes Tulp give an (*) Anatomy Lesson. For ten points, name this profession held by Hayes Agnew and Samuel Gross, who were painted demonstrating surgeries in progress.
parts.answer: doctors (accept equivalents like surgeons or physicians; accept answers describing professors of medicine or professors of surgery; prompt on “teachers” or “professors” by asking “what do they teach?”)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This artist painted himself holding a sword in his armpit in his Self Portrait as the Apostle Paul. This artist holds brushes and a palette in a self portrait that shows him standing in front of two circles. This artist used a brothel as the setting of a painting which depicts himself as the prodigal son along with his wife (*) Saskia. In another painting by this artist, a doctor uses a pair of forceps to pull up the tendons of a corpse’s dissected arm. This artist applied so many layers of varnish to his group portrait of The Shooting Company of Frans Banning Cocq that it now seems like it is set at night. For 10 points, name this Dutch painter of The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp and The Night Watch.

topics.description: American artist known for large-scale, brightly colored blown-glass sculptures and installations inspired by natural forms and gardens.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One artist’s collection of “Persians” of this material are marked with an optic ribbed pattern and brightly-colored “lips.” In works like Dream Garden, an artist embedded color directly in the Favrile form of this material. Nature and gardens inspired many of Dale Chihuly’s large-scale sculptures in this material. (*) Lamps with ornate shades made of this material were designed by Louis Comfort Tiffany. After being melted in a furnace, this material can be blown into shape using a blowpipe. For 10 points, name this material that can be stained with color and is used in windows.
parts.answer: glass [accept Favrile glass or leaded glass or stained glass or glass-blowing]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A kind of this material similar to milk, called lattimo, was made by producers on the Venetian island of Murano. Dale Chihuly is an artist best known for working with this material, which makes up the shade of Tiffany lamps. This material can be shaped by blowing into a hollow clay rod. This material is used in circular “rose” apertures on the walls of many Gothic cathedrals. For 10 points, name this material, which is “stained” in many church windows.

topics.description: French Romantic composer known for Symphonie fantastique, innovative orchestration, programmatic music, and The Damnation of Faust.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This composer took over when a conductor snorted snuff in the middle of the premiere of a piece by him that calls for four offstage brass ensembles. The Rákóczi [rah-KOH-see] March opens this composer’s “dramatic legend” of The Damnation of Faust. This composer profiled over 60 instruments in his Treatise on Instrumentation and Orchestration. An onstage English horn and offstage oboe depict a conversation between two (*) shepherds in a symphony by this composer in which the clarinet carries the idée fixe theme. The final second-to-last movement of that symphony by this composer is called the “March to the Scaffold” and precedes a witches’ sabbath. For 10 points, name this French composer of Symphonie Fantastique.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This work is the second one that its composer marked “quasi una fantasia,” or “like a fantasy.” For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this C-sharp minor piano sonata, whose first movement opens with right-hand triplets. Ludwig Rellstab  compared that movement to light reflecting off of Lake Lucerne.
parts.answer: the Moonlight Sonata [accept, but DO NOT REVEAL, Beethoven’s Piano Sonata No. 14 or  Beethoven’s Opus 27, No. 2]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This deaf German composer of the Moonlight Sonata also wrote Fur Elise.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The quiet first movement repeated pattern of the Moonlight Sonata led this composer to call it a “lamentation.”  This composer also wrote the Symphonie Fantastique.

topics.description: A celebrated fresco panel by Michelangelo on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel depicting God giving life to Adam through nearly touching hands.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One painting in this building depicts souls in the process of being sent to either heaven or hell. In a painting in this building, God reaches out with one finger to give life to the first man. The Last Judgment and The (*) Creation of Adam are frescoes in this church. An artist hired to paint the inside of this church designed a scaffolding system to paint its ceiling. For 10 points, name this church in Vatican City with an interior painted by Michelangelo.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This artist created Rebellious Slave and Dying Slave for the tomb of Pope Julius II, and signed the sash of a sculpture in which a youthful Mary holds the body of Jesus. A contrapposto nude sculpture holding a slingshot and The (*) Creation of Adam are works by this sculptor of the Pieta`. For ten points, name this Italian Renaissance artist who sculpted a marble David and painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
parts.answer: Michelangelo (accept Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni)

topics.description: Rembrandt was a Dutch Golden Age painter and printmaker known for works including The Night Watch, The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp, and Storm on the Sea of Galilee.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This artist painted himself holding a sword in his armpit in his Self Portrait as the Apostle Paul. This artist used a brothel as the setting of a painting which depicts himself as the prodigal son along with his wife (*) Saskia. In another painting by this artist, a doctor uses a pair of forceps to pull up the tendons of a corpse’s dissected arm. This artist applied so many layers of varnish to his group portrait of The Shooting Company of Frans Banning Cocq that it now seems like it is set at night. For 10 points, name this Dutch painter of The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp and The Night Watch.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This artist painted six identically-dressed men in black and white in a painting that became an  iconic symbol of a cigar brand. This artist's only seascape was stolen from the Isabella Stewart  Gardner Museum. This artist of Syndics of the Drapers Guild and Storm on the Sea of Galilee, who  used his wife (*) Saskia as a model, painted a gun blending into feathers on a hat and a girl in a white  dress wearing a dead chicken on her waist. The militia of Frans Banning Cocq (“coke”) was painted by,  for 10 points, what Dutch artist of The Night Watch?

topics.description: Italian composer of comic and serious operas including The Barber of Seville, La Cenerentola, The Thieving Magpie, and William Tell.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In one opera by this composer, the title character sings his name several times in the aria “Largo al Factotum”. One opera by this composer sees a soldier shoot an apple off of Jemmy’s head. That opera’s overture contains a galloping “March of the Swiss Soldiers”. Count Almaviva and Rosina are married while (*) Figaro looks on in one opera by this composer. For 10 points, what Italian wrote music for operas such as The Barber of Seville and William Tell?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In an opera by this composer, Clorinda and Tisbe's father hides Angelina, who falls in love  with Prince Ramiro. This composer wrote an opera in which the female lead sings the aria “Deh!  tu reggi in tal momento” (DEH TOO rej-ee in TAL moh-MAIN-toh) from a scaffold. This composer of  La Cenerentola (lah CHAY-nay-REN-toh-lah) wrote an opera that includes a (*) galop called the  “March of the Swiss Soldiers” and centers on Gessler forcing the protagonist to shoot an arrow through  an apple on Jemmy's head. For 10 points, name this Italian composer of Cinderella, The Thieving  Magpie, and William Tell.

topics.description: A skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and the world's tallest building since its completion.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these structures named Capital Gate holds the record for the furthest leaning manmade building in the world. Fazlur Khan originated a “bundled tube” system used to design these structures while working for Skidmore, Owings, and Merrill. Frank Lloyd Wright designed an unrealized one of these structures called (*) The Illinois. A footbridge connects two of these buildings designed by César Pelli in Kuala Lumpur. Adrian Smith designed one of these buildings in Dubai that includes an unusable spire that adds over 250 yards to its height. For 10 points, the Burj Khalifa and Petronas Twin Towers exemplify what very tall buildings?
parts.answer: skyscrapers [prompt on tower before mention; prompt on high-rise; prompt on office building by asking “What kind of building are the offices located in?”; prompt on hotel by asking “What kind of building is the hotel located in?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The financial crisis of 2008 scuttled plans to finish developing a series of artificial islands in the Persian Gulf, including one set in the shape of the world and several sets in the shape of this plant. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this tropical tree.
parts.answer: palm tree (accept Palm Islands; accept Palm Jumeirah, Palm Jebel Ali, or Palm Deira; accept Arecaceae)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Oil revenue fueled the construction of the Palm artificial islands, which lie off the coast of this most populous city in the United Arab Emirates.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Dubai’s Palm islands lie unfinished, but this tallest building in the world stands nearby and actually was completed in 2009.

topics.description: Animal flesh used as food, including conventional meat and meat produced or emulated through cultivated-meat and plant-based alternatives.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In the early days of the COVID pandemic, reports of a severe shortage of this commodity led to an executive order requiring processing plants to stay open. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general type of commodity whose affected producers included Cargill, Smithfield, JBS, and Tyson.
parts.answer: meat (accept any specific kind of meat, including beef, chicken, and pork; prompt on “food”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The national market for meat is considered an oligopoly because it’s dominated by a small number of firms. In meat’s case, that’s the “Big Five.” If a market only has one major seller, it’s described by this term instead.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The market for this product is also dominated by an oligopoly, led by Abbott Nutrition. After two infants died in early 2022, Abbott issued a recall due to bacterial contamination, and a drastic shortage of this product ensued.
parts.answer: baby formula (accept infant formula; do not prompt on “milk”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Mark Post pioneered the “clean” form of this substance in a proof-of-concept built upon by companies such as Beyond [this substance]. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this substance. One aspect of this substance is emulated by the legume derivative leghemoglobin.
parts.answer: meat [or clean meat; or Beyond Meat]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Some meat substitutes add glutamate to emulate this taste. This taste, which is also known as savoriness, is one of the five tastes along with sweet, sour, salty, and bitter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The textured vegetable protein from this legume is used to emulate the mouthfeel of meat in many meat substitutes. This plant’s bean is used to make tofu.

topics.description: The ionic compound NaCl, commonly encountered as edible salt and naturally occurring as the mineral halite, with major historical importance as a food preservative, seasoning, and traded commodity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: At the Battle of Tondibi, Askia II planned to send a cattle stampede against the armies of this kingdom, but the stampede instead crushed his own men after it panicked due to gunfire. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this kingdom whose ruler Ahmad al-Mansur raided Timbuktu. The Almoravid and Almohad dynasties were centered in this kingdom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] al-Mansur raided this empire, which succeeded Mali as the hegemon of West Africa. It was founded by Askia Muhammad.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Though much of Songhai’s wealth came from gold, it also controlled mines for this good at Taghaza. This mineral was valued in Africa for its using in preserving and flavoring food.
parts.answer: ANSWER: salt [or table salt; or NaCl]

parts.label: L
parts.question: It is said that Rome tilled the ground around Carthage with this resource, so the city would never thrive again. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this resource. The word “salary” comes from money paid to Roman soldiers to buy this resource, which was valuable for its ability to preserve and flavor food.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Romans adopted the use of this other kind of currency from the Greeks. Early Roman forms of these things included the Sestertius and Follis, which were often minted with the current Emperor’s head on one side.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Roman coins lost value during the Crisis of the Third Century due to this economic phenomenon. Emperor Diocletian minted a new coin, the Solidus, to counteract this phenomenon.

topics.description: Haiti is the Caribbean country occupying the western portion of Hispaniola, with Port-au-Prince as its capital.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader originally won his country’s presidential election in 2015, representing the Tet Kale party, but allegations of fraud resulted in a re-contested election in 2016, which he also won. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this world leader who was assassinated in his home in July 2021 by Colombian mercenaries posing as US Drug Enforcement Administration agents. This leader’s wife Martine was also seriously wounded in the attack.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Moise was president of this Caribbean island nation. A devastating magnitude 7.2 earthquake that struck this country in August 2021 had an epicenter 100 miles from its capital of Port-au-Prince (“port-ow-PRANZ”).
parts.answer: Haiti [or Republic of Haiti or Republique d’Haiti or Repiblik d Ayiti]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During his tenure, Moise faced protests over misuse of loans obtained from this country through the Petrocaribe oil alliance. The U.S. recognizes Juan Guaidó as this country’s legitimate president.
parts.answer: Venezuela [or Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela or República Bolivariana de Venezuela]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 2010, this country’s leader, Rene Preval, escaped without injury when the National Palace collapsed ´ in an earthquake that killed over 100,000 people. In July 2021, over two dozen mercenaries carried out the assassination of (*) Jovenel Mo¨ıse, this country’s president. The Duvalier family led this country as despots for much of the 20th century. The island of Hispaniola is shared by the Dominican Republic and, for ten points, what French-speaking Caribbean nation whose capital is Port-au-Prince?
parts.answer: Haiti (accept Republic of Haiti; accept Repiblik d Ayiti; accept Republique d’ ´ Haiti)

topics.description: The Alps are a major mountain range in central and southern Europe, extending from France through Switzerland and Italy to Austria and Slovenia.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This mountain overlooks the resort town of Zermatt. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this notoriously dangerous “Peak of the Meadows,” which lies on the border of Switzerland and Italy. This mountain is partly named for its unique shape, which is a result of the collision of four cirques.
parts.answer: Matterhorn [or Mont Cervin; or Monte Cervino]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Matterhorn is one of this mountain range’s namesake “four-thousanders.” This largest mountain range in Europe runs from France to Slovenia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Zermatt is popular for mountaineering and this other winter sport prevalent in Switzerland. Cities in the United States, such as Telluride and Aspen, are popular resorts for snowboarding and this other activity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The highest mountain in Western Europe, Mont Blanc, is in the western part of this range. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this European mountain range. Mont Blanc lies on the border between Italy and France, before this range stretches to Switzerland.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This major European river has its source in the Swiss Alps; it then flows north, creates much of the border between France and Germany, and empties into the North Sea in the Netherlands.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This iconic, pyramid-shaped Alpine peak lies on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Hundreds of climbers have died on this peak, including four members of the first team to summit it in 1911.

topics.description: A northeastern U.S. state in New England, with Hartford as its capital and a history rooted in the former Connecticut Colony.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After losing one conflict, the name of this tribe was banned and they were forced to assimilate into the Narragansett and Mohegan tribes. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this tribe, which fought the Massachusetts Bay Colony in a namesake 1630s war.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Pequots killed John Stone on this state’s namesake river, helping spark the war. The treaty that ended the war, which banned the Pequot language, was signed in this state’s capital of Hartford.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Before the English arrived in Connecticut, the Pequot primarily traded with merchants from this country, which sold New York to the British for not enough guilders.
parts.answer: Kingdom of The Netherlands [or Holland; Koninkrijk der Nederlanden]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The “blue lights” gathered in this state to participate in an event presided over by George  Cabot. Joseph Wadsworth protected a document named for this state from Edmund Andros,  which was co-written by Thomas Hooker. This state's Royal Charter was hidden in the (*) Charter  Oak. A bicameral legislature balancing the interests of small and large states was included in a  compromise named for this state proposed by Roger Sherman. A meeting of Federalists who opposed  the War of 1812 took place in, for 10 points, what state's city of Hartford?

topics.description: The modern country in northwestern South America, whose capital is Bogotá.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The vast majority of volcanoes that erupt this substance can be found in the Gobustan State Reserve in Azerbaijan. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this substance that floods areas in namesake “slides” as lahars after volcanic events. This substance that typically forms after rainfall is a mixture of soil and water.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The mud volcanoes at Gobustan State Reserve can be found near Azerbaijan’s coastline on this body of water. The Volga River has its mouth in this inland sea, which is technically the world’s largest lake.

parts.label: C

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this author of One Hundred Years of Solitude. Because his name is Spanish, he has two surnames, the first inherited from his father and the second from his mother; therefore, the first of his two last names is required.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Gabriel Garc´ıa Marquez is from this South American country, where ´ One Hundred Years of Solitude is set. Its capital is Bogota.´
parts.answer: Colombia (accept Republic of Colombia or Republica de ´ Colombia)

parts.question: The seventh generation of the Buend´ıa family is made up entirely of a baby boy, Aureliano, who has the tail of one of these animals. In the novel Charlotte’s Web, Wilbur is one of these animals.

topics.description: A large urban park in Manhattan, New York City, designed primarily by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Characters in this play play party games such as “Hump the Hostess” and “Get the Guests.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this play, in which the younger couple Nick and Honey visit the home of George and Martha. At the end of this play, Martha exclaims “I am!” in response to the title question.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This author of Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? depicted a conversation between the humans Nancy and Charlie and the reptiles Leslie and Sarah in Seascape.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Jerry asks “Could I have planned all this?” after impaling himself on a knife held by Peter in an Edward Albee play set in this location, a large park in Manhattan.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The artists Christo and Jeanne-Claude installed 5,703 fabric-covered gates in this place in 2005. Features called the Lake and the Ramble are in this place, whose layout was primarily designed by Frederick Law Olmstead. This place, which divides the Upper West and Upper East Sides of (*) Manhattan, is the origin of Shakespeare in the Park. For ten points, name this large park in New York City.
parts.answer: Central Park [prompt on Manhattan Island; prompt on New York City or NYC]

topics.description: A city on Alaska’s Seward Peninsula and the western terminus of the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the Iditarod, a large sled dog race. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this state, where the Iditarod takes place. This state’s capital is Juneau.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Although Juneau is Alaska’s capital, it is not on the Iditarod route. Instead, the race begins in this most  populous city in Alaska.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Sled dogs race for nearly one thousand miles before the Iditarod ends in this Western Alaska city on the Seward  Peninsula.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the geography of the Iditarod [“eye”-dih-tah-rod], for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The Iditarod is an annual sled dog race that takes place over hundreds of miles in this US state.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Iditarod begins in this most populous Alaskan city which, due to its polar location and size, is home to the surprisingly busy Ted Stevens International Airport.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Iditarod ends in this town on the southern tip of the Seward Peninsula.

topics.description: A major river of Mesopotamia flowing through or along Turkey, Syria, and Iraq, including Baghdad, and forming one of the region's defining rivers alongside the Euphrates.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Elamite and Akkadian are among the languages that were written in this system despite not being native languages of the civilization that invented it. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this writing system, developed by the Sumerians, that uses a reed stylus to make wedge-shaped impressions on clay tablets.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Sumerians and Babylonians flourished in this region with a Greek name. This region in the “fertile crescent” was a center of early agriculture, since the plow was invented here.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Mesopotamia is Greek for “the land between the rivers;” specifically, between the Euphrates [yoo-fray-tees] and this other major Middle Eastern river.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The region of Mesopotamia was home to some of the first civilizations in the world. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Mesopotamia was able to sustain large populations due to the ease of this practice. This practice is the cultivation of crops.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This Mesopotamian civilization contained the city of Ashur and had rulers like Tigaleth-Pileser and Sennacherib. Its capital, Nineveh (NIN-ih-veh), hosted the largest library in the world at the time, built by Ashurbanipal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Mesopotamia was known as the Fertile Crescent for the rich soil that the Euphrates (yoo-FRAY-tees) and this other river provided to the region. Baghdad lies on this river.

topics.description: A seawater inlet between northeastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, connecting the Mediterranean region through the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba to the Gulf of Aden.

parts.question: In the Quran, this religious figure is shocked to see the wise man al-Khidr cut a hole in a boat, kill a young man, and rebuild a wall. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this man who learns about the will of Allah from al-Khidr and who, in the book of Leviticus, receives numerous holy laws from Yahweh.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Before receiving the laws outlined in Leviticus, Moses receives this short set of rules from Yahweh while atop Mount Sinai. These rules include the directions not to kill and not to commit adultery.
parts.answer: Ten Commandments (accept Decalogue; accept Aseret ha’Dibrot; prompt on “Commandments” or “Dibrot” alone)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Earlier in his life, Moses follows Yahweh’s instructions to part and then close this waterway while he leads the Israelites out of Egypt.
parts.answer: Red Sea (accept Yam Suf; accept hayyam ha’adom; accept al-Bahr al-Ahmar)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Twenty miles north of this city is a series of sandstone cliffs in Timna Park, which is accessed by the  nearby Ramon Airport. For 10 points each:

parts.question: Name this southernmost city in Israel. Outside this city on the Gulf of Aqaba (AH-kuh-bah), visitors  can ride camels in the Southern Negev (NEG-ev).

parts.label: B
parts.question: Eilat is at the northern tip of this body of water, which separates Egypt from Saudi Arabia and  borders Sudan and Yemen.
parts.answer: Red Sea [or al-Baḥr al-ʾAḥmar or Yam Sūf]

parts.label: C
parts.question: A high-speed railway will soon connect Eilat to Beersheba (bair-SHAY-bah) and this other city, the  technology center of Israel, which forms a metroplex with Yafo (YAH-foh).

topics.description: Lord Byron, formally George Gordon Byron, was an English Romantic poet known for works including Don Juan, Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage, and “The Destruction of Sennacherib.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This poet’s rivalry with John Keats was so intense that he used the poem Don Juan [don JOO-an] to mock him after death, claiming that Keats had died from reading a bad review of his work instead of from tuberculosis. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this English Romantic poet. Keats was convinced that this nobleman had bought good reviews for works like Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage.
parts.answer: Lord Byron (accept George Gordon, Lord Byron; accept George Gordon Noel Byron, sixth Baron Byron)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Keats wrote many of his own poems in this poetic style, in which the author directly addresses a subject. Keats wrote poems of this type “on a Grecian Urn” and “to a Nightingale.”
parts.answer: odes (accept Ode on a Grecian Urn; accept Ode to a Nightingale)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Byron died in Missolonghi, and became a national hero during this country’s war of independence. This Mediterranean country is led from Athens.
parts.answer: Greece (accept Hellenic Republic; accept Ellada´ or Hellas; accept Ellinik´ı Dimokrat´ıa)

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem by this author, the speaker says, “There is grief in the sound, there is guilt in the fame” because “I Speak Not, I Trace Not, I Breathe Not Thy Name.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this poet, who described how “the Angel of Death spread his wings on the blast” and “[t]he Assyrian came down like the wolf on the fold” in the poem “The Destruction of Sennacherib.”
parts.answer: Lord Byron [or George Gordon Byron, 6th Baron Byron]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In this poem by Byron, the title action is done “like the night / Of cloudless climes and starry skies [as] all that’s best of dark and bright / Meet in her aspect and her eyes.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Byron dedicated a tale in verse titled for “The Prophecy of [this author]” to Countess Teresa Guiccioli. This author described a woman named Beatrice guiding him through Paradiso in The Divine Comedy.

topics.topic: To a Mouse, on Turning Her Up in Her Nest with the Plough
topics.description: A poem by Robert Burns in which a plough-disturbed mouse's nest prompts reflections on human disruption of nature and the uncertainty of future plans.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this poem, the speaker apologizes that “Man’s dominion / Has broken Nature’s social union.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this poem, which tells the title figure, “thou art no thy-lane, / In proving foresight may be vain” when things “Gang aft agley.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This author of “To A Mouse” compared his “Luve” to “the melody… sweetly played in tune” in the poem“A Red, Red Rose.”

parts.question: [E] Burns also wrote this poem, which asks, “Should old acquaintance be forgot” and is usually sung at the stroke of midnight on New Year's Eve.

parts.question: Romantic poet Robert Burns wrote about people with this nationality “wha hae wi’ Wallace bled” and “wham Bruce has aften led.” For ten points each,

parts.question: Name this European nation, Burns’s homeland, whose dialect he used to write about schemes that “gang aft agley.”
parts.answer: Scottish (accept Scots English; accept Scotland; accept Alba)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Burns wrote “the best-laid schemes o’ [these creatures] an’ men / gang aft agley” in a poem addressed to one of these small mammals when he “[Turned] Her Up in Her Nest With the Plough.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Burns also used the Scots dialect to write this poem, often sung at New Year’s, which asks “should ault acquaintance be forgot / and never brought to mind?”

parts.question: Name this American poet who frequently edited and republished his poetry collection Leaves of Grass.

parts.question: The “great star early droop’d in the western sky” in a Whitman poem named for these springtime flowers “with heart-shaped leaves of rich green” and “many a pointed blossom.”
parts.answer: Lilacs (accept When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d)

topics.description: Ralph Ellison's 1952 novel follows an unnamed Black narrator whose social invisibility reflects racism, political manipulation, and the racial realities of the United States.

parts.question: In this novel, one character dreams of a nude woman trying to "keep [him] out of the clock" before he has sex with his daughter Matty Lou. parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The narrator of this novel is reminded of Louis Armstrong’s song “Black and Blue” while imagining talking to a slave woman mourning her master’s death. At the end of this novel, the narrator kills Ras the Destroyer during the race riot and falls through a manhole into a hidden underground room. topics.description: Alexandre Dumas père was a French novelist known for adventure works including The Count of Monte Cristo and The Three Musketeers.

parts.question: The protagonist of this novel takes revenge on the Count de Morcerf Fernand, the wealthy banker Danglars, and the prosecutor for the king Villefort. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novel. An old man called the “Mad Priest” helps the protagonist of this novel escape the Château d'If (SHA-toe DEEF), where he was imprisoned after being framed for being a Bonapartist traitor.

parts.question: [M] The Count of Monte Cristo was written by this French author. This author wrote Twenty Years After and The Vicomte of Bragelonne (vee-COMT of BRAH-jehl-uhn) as sequels to one of his most famous novels.

parts.question: Name this protagonist of an 1844 adventure novel who encounters the swashbuckling Athos, Porthos, and Aramis.

parts.question: This author wrote about the title talking cat, which angers guests at a dinner party by spreading overheard gossip,  in his short story “Tobermory.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this author, who ends his short story “The Open Window” with the line “romance at short notice was her  specialty.”

parts.question: This character lost two fingernails on his right hand after escaping from a gang of Snatchers and claiming to be Stan Shunpike. parts.answer: Romeo and Juliet (accept The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet)

parts.question: This poet wrote a collection that declares “tonight, I can write the saddest lines,” and that ends with a poem that laments “in you, everything sank.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this poet of Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair.
parts.answer: Pablo Neruda (accept Ricardo Eliecer Neftal ´ ´ı Reyes Basoalto)

parts.question: Bernardo is a stand-in for Leonardo da Vinci in a novel from this country in which the prince of an Italian city-state is advised by the title dwarf. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this country. In a chamber play from this country, the ghost of a milkmaid haunts the vengeful, wheelchair-bound Jacob Hummel.
parts.answer: Sweden [or Kingdom of Sweden or Sverige or Konungariket Sverige] (The first novel is The Dwarf by Pär Lagerkvist.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] That play, The Ghost Sonata, is by this Swedish author. The title character’s pet canary is decapitated by the valet Jean in this author’s play Miss Julie.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The author of The Dwarf, Pär Lagerkvist, is among the eight Swedish authors who have won this prize, which is awarded by the Swedish Academy. More recent recipients of this prize include Louise Glück and Bob Dylan.

topics.description: The problem of determining the exact value of the infinite series of reciprocals of the positive integer squares, equal to π²/6.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This number squared over six is the solution to the Basel problem, which concerns an infinite  sum of inverse squares. E raised to this number times i is equal to negative one according to  Euler's (OY-lur's) identity. Squaring the circle is an impossible task because this number is (*) transcendental. This number is the period of the tangent function, and this number of radians is equal to  180 degrees. This irrational number is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter. For 10 points,  name this number that is approximately equal to 3.14.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Basel problem deals with the sum of the reciprocals of these numbers, which Euler proved is equal to pi squared over 6. The differences between these numbers are increasing consecutive (*) odd numbers. These are the only integers with an odd number of factors. For 10 points, name these numbers that are equal to another number times itself.
parts.answer: square numbers [or perfect squares; prompt on perfect powers]

topics.description: A mathematical limit is the value that a function or sequence approaches as its input or index approaches a specified value or infinity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The squeeze theorem can be used to calculate this value for a function that is trapped in between two  other functions. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this value that a function approaches without necessarily reaching.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This rule is used to find limits for indeterminate forms, such as infinity over infinity.
parts.answer: ANSWER: L'Hôpital's (LOH-peet-aal's) rule [or L'Hospital's rule; or Bernoulli's rule]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] A function has this property at a point if the limit of the function, as it approaches that point, exists  and is equal to the function at that point.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The absolute value function has this property everywhere, except at x = 0. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this property that is possessed everywhere by smooth functions, since they have a tangent line at every point. Functions with this property are continuous, but the opposite is not always true.
parts.answer: differentiability [accept word forms like differentiable; accept anything involving having a derivative]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The concept of continuity can be rigorously defined using these constructs. These constructs are values a function approaches as its input approaches some value. They are denoted by “lim.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Limits don’t exist at the “vertical” examples of these things, which are lines that a function approaches, but never reaches. The graph of a hyperbola has two diagonal examples of these things.

topics.description: The geometric relationship in which figures have the same shape and size, with corresponding parts congruent.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one of this man’s dialogues, he claimed that the classical elements were composed of his namesake solids. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Greek philosopher who names a group of five convex, regular polyhedra including the tetrahedron and the cube.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] An Octahedron, one of the Platonic solids, has this many faces. An octagon has this many sides.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The faces of regular polyhedra have this property. The sides of regular polygons also have this property.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some alternative, less-official names for this shape include diamond and lozenge, which some textbooks use for examples with specific angle measures. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for a quadrilateral whose four sides are all the same length.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A square is a special type of rhombus with an extra requirement. In a rhombus, each pair of opposite angles must have this relationship, but in a square, all four angles must have this relationship to each other.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Because a rhombus has pairs of congruent opposite sides, a rhombus is a parallelogram. A rhombus also has pairs of congruent adjacent sides, which makes it this type of quadrilateral that shares its name and general shape with a common toy.

topics.description: The probability-weighted average of a random variable’s possible outcomes, also called its expectation or first moment.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Sequences where the value of one term is equal to this quantity for the next term are called “martingales.” The moment-generating function of a random variable X is computed by finding this quantity for “e to the t X”. For a random variable x with PDF f of x, this quantity equals [read slowly] “the integral from minus infinity to infinity of x times f of x dx.” The law of large numbers states that for a large number of trials, the (*) mean result will approach this value. When rolling a six-sided die, this value for the outcome is 3.5 (“3 point 5”). For 10 points, name this term for the average predicted value of a random variable, often denoted “E of X.”
parts.answer: expected value [or expectation; accept just expected after “value” is read; accept EV; accept conditional expectation; accept mean or average before “mean” but prompt afterwards; accept E(X) (“E of X”) before it is read]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Regardless of whether the variables are independent, this operator is always linear. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this operator, which returns the integral of x times f of x for a probability distribution. When rolling a fair die, this value is 3.5.
parts.answer: expectation operator [or expected value; accept first moment; prompt on average or center]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The expected value is calculated for variables of this type, which represent uncertainty or chance. Variables of this type include the flip or a coin or the roll of a die.
parts.answer: random variables [accept stochastic or aleatory variables; accept pseudorandom variables]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This law predicts that the expected value will converge to the arithmetic mean as the number of samples increases.

topics.description: The logarithm to base e, commonly denoted ln, and the antiderivative of 1/x on intervals not containing zero.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This function is differentiable everywhere, except at x equals 0. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this function denoted with two vertical bars, which converts a negative number to its positive counterpart.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The derivative of the absolute value for x less than zero is this value, while the derivative for x greater than zero  is this other value. Name both, and it may help to know the derivative is equal to the slope for this function.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The anti-derivative of the function “one over x” equals this function of the absolute value of x, plus C.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Hess's law can be used to calculate the total change of this quantity in a reaction. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this quantity, which is equal to the internal energy plus the product of pressure and volume. It is symbolized H.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This quantity can be calculated by subtracting the product of temperature and entropy from enthalpy. This quantity is named for an American scientist and can be used to determine if a reaction is spontaneous.
parts.answer: Gibbs free energy [prompt on free energy]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The change in Gibbs free energy can be calculated by taking the negative product of this function of the equilibrium constant and RT. This function is symbolized “ln” and is a logarithm with the base of e.

topics.description: A Chinese technology company that owns TikTok and operates other internet-content and social-media services.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This app is known in China as “Douyin.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this social media app that consists of short videos, often of people doing dances dubbed with music or other audio recordings.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This page on TikTok recommends videos to users based on the way the user interacts with the app. This page is located to the right of the “following” page.

In August 2020, Donald Trump issued an order banning transactions with this platform’s parent company, ByteDance, and encouraged it to be bought by a "very (*) American" company like Microsoft. For 10 points, name this video-sharing app which has been criticized for associations with China.

topics.description: A French electronic music duo consisting of Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, known for helmeted robot imagery and songs such as “One More Time,” “Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger,” and “Get Lucky.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The British music magazine NME named this band’s debut album, Is This It, as the best album of the 2000s. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this alt-rock band who included songs like “Brooklyn Bridge to Chorus” and “Ode to the Mets” on their aptly-named 2020 album The New Abnormal.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Strokes frontman Julian Casablancas collaborated with this French band on the song “Instant Crush”. Their other songs include “Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger”, “One More Time”, and “Get Lucky”, the latter of which appeared on their album Random Access Memories.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Casablancas's side project The Voidz released the album Virtue in 2018, which includes a song titled for an ocean of this color. A band partially named for this color released albums such as The Dark Side of the Moon and The Wall.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A choir singing “Hold on / if love is the answer / you’re home” appears on this group’s song “Touch.” Another song by this group has disco producer Giorgio Moroder talking about his career in place of lyrics. Those songs, along with “Lose Yourself to Dance,” appear on this group’s album (*) Random Access Memories. One song by this group states “work it, make it, do it, makes us” before listing the title four adjectives. Another song by this group states “we’re up all night to the sun.” For 10 points, name this electronic music duo that disbanded in 2021, known for their iconic helmets and songs like “Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger,” and “Get Lucky.”

topics.description: An iconic Disney cartoon mouse character who debuted in the 1928 animated short Steamboat Willie.

parts.question: Takashi Murakami, an artist from this country, often depicted its otaku subculture in works from its Superflat  movement. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country, whose history of visual flatness traces back to Hokusai’s prints depicting Thirty-Six Views of  Mount Fuji.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The shape of Murakami’s signature character, Mr. DOB, is reminiscent of this animated character. The 1928  film Steamboat Willie saw this character’s first film appearance.

topics.description: A satyr is a masculine woodland or nature spirit in Greek mythology, typically depicted with human features and animal attributes such as goat ears, legs, horns, or a tail, and associated with music and revelry.

parts.question: Some myths about the invention of one of these items credits Hermes with making it using a tortoise’s shell and entrails. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these items, which were used in a contest where Midas was given donkey ears for ruling against one god. That god, the son of Leto, often used one of these items called a lyre.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The lyre was a favorite instrument of this Greek god of music, the twin brother of Artemis.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The aforementioned musical contest was between Apollo and one of these beings. Another one of these hybrid beings, Marsyas, was flayed when he lost a music contest to Apollo because he couldn't play his flute upside down.

parts.question: Name some types of humanoid creatures with animal attributes from Greek myth, for ten points each.

parts.question: One of these creatures, Chiron, taught both Jason and Achilles. Chiron was unusual among these creatures because his front pair of feet were often depicted as human, and only his back two feet were horse hoofs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Naiads and dryads were two types of these feminine nature spirits. Echo was one of these creatures.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In art, nymphs have often been depicted frolicking with these masculine nature spirits that had the ears and legs of goats, similar to the god Pan.
parts.answer: satyr (accept satyros; accept faun; accept silenos)

topics.description: The body of Jewish dietary laws governing which foods may be eaten and how they are prepared.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This decentralized religion has many “mansions” like the Nyabinghi, the Bobo Ashanti, and the Twelve Tribes of Israel. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Afrocentric Abrahamic religion that developed in Jamaica during the early 1900s. Many followers of this religion believe that the Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie I was the second coming of Christ.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Followers of the Rastafarian Movement refer to God by this name. This name comes from a short form of the Hebrew tetragrammaton, the personal name of God used by the ancient Israelites.

parts.question: [E] Followers of the Rastafarian Movement also abide by the i-tal one of these restrictions. Kosher foods refer to those that conform to the kashrut, the Jewish one of these general restrictions on food that one can eat.

parts.question: The shechita process is required for some items to have this status. If meat and dairy products are mixed, the resulting meal cannot have this property. No cloven-hoofed mammals can have this status, which is why observant (*) Jews abstain from eating pork. The Hebrew word for "fit" describes, for 10 points, what status given to foods in accordance with Jewish dietary law?
parts.answer: being kosher [accept anything related to obeying kashrut; prompt on descriptive answers like “Jews can eat it”]

topics.topic: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
topics.description: Joseph Campbell’s 1949 comparative mythology study presenting the monomyth, or hero’s journey, as a recurring narrative pattern.
aliases: The Hero with a Thousand Faces: The Collected Works of Joseph Campbell

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about amateur mythologist Lord Raglan:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Along with Otto Rank, Raglan names an archetype for this type of character involving 22 plot points. Another archetype, the monomyth, is known as the “Journey” of this type of character.
parts.answer: hero [or heroes; accept Hero’s Journey or mythic hero]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Raglan’s ideas were built upon in this work of comparative mythology by Joseph Campbell, which identifies a descent and return from the Underworld as part of the monomyth archetype.
parts.answer: The Hero With a Thousand Faces

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] One of the heroes who deviated the most from Raglan’s original 22-plot-point archetype was this outlaw, who led the Merry Men against the Duke of Nottingham in English folk tales.

parts.question: This director used footage from an erupting Mount Etna in a setting that represents a character’s descent to Hell. The climax of this director’s breakout film pays homage to a battle scene from The Dam Busters, while the film’s opening draws from Kurosawa’s The Hidden Fortress by following two unassuming characters. This director applied the monomyth from (*) The Hero with a Thousand Faces to the genre of action films. This director of American Graf iti chose James Earl Jones to voice an iconic villain and hired John Williams to compose scores that include the “Imperial March.” For 10 points, name this director of Star Wars.
parts.answer: George Lucas [or George Walton Lucas Jr.]

topics.description: The legendary magical sword associated with King Arthur in Arthurian tradition.

parts.question: This man's sword had a scabbard which prevented its wearer from bleeding from any wounds. This man was mortally wounded despite defeating Mordred at the Battle of Camlann. This son of Uther (*) Pendragon was served by the wizard Merlin and the Knights of the Round Table. For 10 points, what legendary English king wielded Excalibur and pulled a sword from a stone?
parts.answer: King Arthur [or Arthur Pendragon; prompt on Pendragon until it is read]

parts.question: After the Sword in the Stone is broken in a fight, one figure receives this sword from an enchantress. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this magical sword wielded by a King of Camelot who is advised by Merlin.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Excalibur is wielded by this mythical British king, who is served by the Knights of the Round Table.

parts.label: C

parts.question: A giant crab was sent to distract a hero and his nephew Iolaus while they were fighting this creature. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [M] Name this creature that inhabited a lake in Lerna. This creature was defeated when flaming arrows prevented its heads from regenerating.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Defeating the Hydra was part of the Twelve Labors of this hero.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Another of the Labors involved capturing one of these creatures from Erymanthos, which Hercules accomplished by first driving it into the snow. Another of these creatures ravaged Calydon before Meleager killed it.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The centaurs Hylaeus and Rhaecus attempted to assault this hero during an event caused by a failure to  honor Artemis. This woman and her husband were turned into lions for sleeping in the temple of Zeus.  Meleager gave this woman the pelt of the (*) Calydonian Boar after she drew first blood in its hunt. For 10 points,  name this huntress, who married Hippomenes after he distracted her with golden apples during a footrace.

topics.description: The underworld in K’iche’ Maya mythology, ruled by death gods and featured prominently in the Popol Vuh.

parts.question: The legend of Hunahpu and Xbalanque [hoo-nah-poo and sh’bah-LAHN-kay] is the subject of one of these peoples’ oldest myths. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Mesoamerican civilization whose myths and history are recorded in the Popol Vuh. These people built the city of Chichen Itza on the Yucatan Peninsula.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Hunahpu and Xbalanque are one of several pairs of heroes in American mythologies that have this familial relationship.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In the myth, the Hero Twins are summoned to this Mayan underworld, where they play the ball game and trick the lords of this place, One Death and Seven Death, into being sacrificed.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This civilization’s gods of death include the “Obsidian Butterfly,” Itzpapalotl [EETZ-pah-pah-lah-toll], and the bat Camazotz. The Popol Vuh was a sacred text of this civilization, and describes underworld (*) Xibalba [shee-BAL-ba]. Priests wore the pelts of jaguars in, for ten points, what meso-american civilization, whose “long count” calendar reset in 2012?
parts.answer: Mayan civilization (accept Mayans or Mayan Empire)

topics.description: The central Christian prayer taught by Jesus, beginning with an address to God as “Our Father in heaven.”

parts.question: [E] In addition to beads, rosaries include a small depiction of one of these objects, one of which Jesus died on.

parts.question: Jesus first recited these phrases as a part of a period of preaching in Galilee shortly after he was baptised. For ten points each:

parts.question: [H] Name these blessings, the first of which is “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.” These proverb-like proclamations were first recounted in the Sermon on the Mount.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Beatitudes and the Sermon on the Mount are first mentioned in Matthew, which is one of these Biblical books. Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John are the four canonical books of this kind, whose name translates to “good news”.

parts.question: [M] The Sermon on the Mount also serves as the first mention of this prayer in the Bible. This prayer begins “Our father in heaven, hallowed be your name.”
parts.answer: Lord’s Prayer [prompt on Our Father or Pater Noster]

topics.description: A major Hindu goddess, consort of Shiva and mother of Ganesha and Karthikeya, regarded as the rebirth or form of Sati.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This god was created out of turmeric paste to guard his mother during a bath. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Hindu god, who is celebrated in a namesake “Chaturthi” festival. This elephant-headed “remover of  obstacles” defeated his brother Karthikeya in a race around the world by encircling his parents.
parts.answer: Ganesha [or Ganapati; or Vinayaka; or Pillaiyar]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ganesha was created by this goddess, his mother. This goddess’ form, Sati, is the etiology of a Hindu funerary  ritual.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Ganesha and Karthikeya were both sons of this Hindu destroyer god, who makes up the Trimurti with Vishnu  and Brahma.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the different forms of the Hindu god Shiva, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] In his hermaphrodite form Ardhanarishvara [uhr-duh-nuh-REESH-vuh-ruh], Shiva is combined with this other god. This goddess was born after Sati [SUH-tee] threw herself into a funeral pyre.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Shiva is often depicted riding Nandi [NUN-dee], a white one of these animals. The slaughter of these animals is taboo across many Hindu states in India.
parts.answer: cows [accept cattle; accept bull; accept steer]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In his Nataraja [NUH-tuh-rah-juh] form, Shiva performs this action. Kali performs this action on top of Shiva in an attempt to destroy the world.
parts.answer: dancing [accept the Lord of the Dance]

topics.description: A title for spiritual leaders in Sikhism, culminating in the eternal authority of the Guru Granth Sahib after the human Gurus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the “Thieves” of Sikhism:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] There are this number of thieves that represent various sins. Sikhs carry a kangha comb and uncut hair called kesh as two of this number of “K’s” to signify their faith.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The counterpart to the Five Thieves are the Five Virtues, traits one must develop in order to reach this state of liberation or enlightenment. In Sikhism, this state can break the cycle of rebirths and karma, similar to the concept of nirvana in Buddhism.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] One way of overcoming the evils of the Thieves in Sikhism is to learn from one of these figures. This four-letter term that refers to the spiritual leaders of Sikhism like Nanak has become a synonym for teacher.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One holder of this title challenged people to point him to where God is not after pointing his feet toward the Kaaba. That holder of this title threw his bowl in a sewer to find a successor. The first person to hold this title declared, “there is no Hindu, there is no Muslim.” The last person to hold this title founded an order called the (*) Khalsa and told his followers to obey the Five Ks. The last human to hold this title, Gobind Singh, declared that the eternal holder of this title would be a book called Granth Sahib. The first person to hold this title was named Nanak. For 10 points, give the title for religious leaders in Sikhism, derived from the Sanskrit word for “mentor.”

topics.description: The religious and ethical principle of nonviolence toward living beings, especially central to Jainism.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Female nuns of one of this religion’s sects cannot attain aparigraha because they are not allowed to be nude. That sect of this religion, the “sky-clad” Digambaras, differs from the “white-clad” Svetambara sect. This religion venerates 24 spiritual leaders called tirthankaras, the last of whom was Mahavira. For 10 points, name this religion, whose adherents practice a vow of nonviolence called ahimsa.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Uncooked rice, coconut shells, and dry almonds are part of the eight articles followers of this religion focus prayer through.
